original_question: In the q-coloring model on bounded-degree graphs, what is the sharp threshold in q versus Delta separating guaranteed uniqueness from possible nonuniqueness of infinite-volume Gibbs measures? In particular, is the classical q>2Delta condition sharp, or can the true borderline be as low as q>Delta (as suggested by tree behavior)?
target_in_paper: Your draft is targeting the paper’s main uniqueness conjecture for the q-coloring model: namely, whether the zero-temperature antiferromagnetic Potts model on infinite graphs of maximum degree Δ has unique Gibbs measure already in the tree-threshold regime q>Δ, rather than only under the classical Dobrushin-type sufficient condition q>2Δ. The nearby official context is the paper’s Conjecture 1.1, read together with Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3, which calibrate the conjecture against the regular-tree threshold. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0004231))
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the right model class (q-colorings / zero-temperature antiferromagnetic Potts), the right phenomenon (uniqueness versus nonuniqueness of infinite-volume Gibbs measures), the right comparison bound (the classical q>2Δ uniqueness condition), and the right source of evidence for a sharper threshold (the regular-tree behavior). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0004231))
missing_details: It should explicitly say that the model is the q-coloring model, i.e. the zero-temperature antiferromagnetic q-state Potts model with uniform activities, so that finite-volume conditional laws are uniform over proper q-colorings compatible with the boundary condition. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0004231))

It should specify the quantifiers: uniqueness is to hold for every infinite graph G of maximum degree Δ, whereas nonuniqueness means that there exists at least one such infinite graph (in the paper’s calibration, the regular tree) with more than one Gibbs measure. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167715202000548?utm_source=openai))

It should state that q and Δ are integers (with q≥2 and Δ≥2 in the natural regime), rather than treating q and Δ as informal continuous parameters. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10955-023-03145-z))

The tree comparison should be made precise: for the (r+1)-regular tree, the nonuniqueness side is q≤r+1 and the uniqueness side is q≥r+2; rewritten in terms of maximum degree Δ=r+1, this is exactly the borderline between q≤Δ and q≥Δ+1. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167715202000548?utm_source=openai))

The phrase “classical q>2Δ condition” should be clarified as a sufficient condition coming from the Dobrushin uniqueness theorem / Salas–Sokal bound, not as the conjectured sharp threshold. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9603068?utm_source=openai))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should say explicitly that it concerns uniqueness of infinite-volume Gibbs measures, not stronger notions such as strong spatial mixing, rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics, or zero-freeness of the partition function. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0004231))
refined_question: Let G be an infinite graph of maximum degree Δ, and consider the q-coloring model on G (equivalently, the zero-temperature antiferromagnetic q-state Potts model with uniform activities), where a Gibbs measure means an infinite-volume DLR measure whose finite-volume conditional distributions are uniform on proper q-colorings compatible with the boundary condition. Is it true that for every integer Δ≥2 and every integer q>Δ there is a unique Gibbs measure on every such G? In other words, is the sharp general uniqueness threshold q_c(Δ)=Δ+1, matching the regular-tree threshold (nonuniqueness possible for q≤Δ and uniqueness on the infinite Δ-regular tree for q≥Δ+1), rather than the older sufficient bound q>2Δ coming from the Dobrushin method? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167715202000548?utm_source=openai))
justification: This is the narrowest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft because the paper is explicitly about the q-coloring model / zero-temperature antiferromagnetic Potts model and its infinite-volume Gibbs measures, not about broader spatial-mixing or algorithmic questions. The relevant local context is exactly the comparison between the Dobrushin/Salas–Sokal sufficient bound q>2Δ and the regular-tree threshold: the regular tree supplies the sharp lower-side obstruction via frozen colorings when q is too small, while the tree uniqueness theorem gives uniqueness once q reaches the tree threshold. Conjecture 1.1 is therefore best rendered as asking whether the tree threshold q=Δ+1 is already the correct threshold for guaranteed uniqueness on all infinite graphs of maximum degree Δ. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0004231))
